In the highly urban areas of the projects, impacts on fish and wildlife values are less than in other localities. In each case, however, fish and wildlife impacts should be minimized and if possible the projects should include measures to enhance those values. In particular project demolition and construction should be accomplished so as to avoid or minimize siltation and sedimentation. Trees and shrubs which must be removed should be replaced to provide habitat, including, where appropriate, food, for small mammals and birds. We are pleased to note that a wildlife sanctuary is being developed as part of the Kingston Urban Renewal Project.
These projects are being undertaken in urbanized areas where recreation needs and opportunities are particularly important because of demographic and economic characteristics of the populations. Urban renewal projects of the type proposed present unique opportunities to ensure that sufficient recreation and open space areas are included to meet those needs. In this regard, each statement should specifically identify relevant municipal open space and recreation plans and standards and then relate project design to those plans. We are pleased that the projects generally provide for recreation and open space. However, the adequacy of such cannot be determined without discussing the relationships of existing open space plans and the needs of the community.
Additionally, we are concerned, in a broader sense, with the long range implications of rebuilding within the 100 year flood plains. To do so will ensure that we incur future flood losses. The statements generally recognize this fact and several propose no additional structures within project boundaries. This is consistent with the intent of Executive Order 11296.
We recognize that because of historical growth, location and current social and economic development, it may not be realistic or feasible to eliminate all development within the 100 year flood plain of the projects. However, we believe that all efforts should be taken to reduce to a minimum incompatible developments on flood plains and thus reduce future flood losses. We suggest that each project be reviewed to determine if all possible measures have been taken to accomplish this goal.
(Mrs.) ELLEN M. JENSON
Acting Special Assistant to the Secretary
